title_topic: Pulmonary embolism with right ventricular failure
summary: A consultant-level look at intermediate-high and high-risk pulmonary embolism. PEITHO (NEJM 2014, 1,005 patients) found that full-dose tenecteplase cut death or haemodynamic decompensation at 7 days from 5.6% to 2.6%. It raised extracranial bleeding (6.3% vs 1.2%) and stroke (2.4% vs 0.2%), with no mortality benefit at 30 days or at about 3 years. ESC 2019 therefore reserved systemic lysis for high-risk PE and for rescue. Reduced-dose lysis is common in UK practice (ERUPT audit), but the outcome trial, PEITHO-3, has not yet reported. HI-PEITHO (NEJM 2026, 544 patients) is the first RCT in which a catheter therapy beat anticoagulation alone on a clinical composite: 4.0% vs 10.3% at 7 days, RR 0.39, with no intracranial haemorrhage. The benefit was driven by decompensation, though, and 14 of the 28 control-arm events met only the NEWS of 9 or more criterion. The trial was open-label and industry-funded, and 30-day deaths were 6 vs 3. PEERLESS, STORM-PE and CANARY measured mostly process or surrogate outcomes. The 2026 AHA/ACC guideline introduced categories A to E. It makes systemic lysis, catheter therapy and surgery all reasonable in category E1 and possible in category D, and gives PERT a class 1 recommendation, but its evidence review predates HI-PEITHO. NICE NG158 still says not to lyse stable patients. Supportive care means cautious fluid, early noradrenaline, high-flow oxygen and treating intubation as peri-arrest. VA-ECMO is a bridge, with observational pooled mortality of about 43%. UK surgical embolectomy is rare and carries about 25% in-hospital mortality.
takeaways: Full-dose systemic lysis prevents collapse in intermediate-risk PE but increases bleeding and haemorrhagic stroke and doesn't reduce mortality: keep it for shock or deterioration.

HI-PEITHO supports catheter-directed lysis for intermediate-high-risk patients with tachycardia, tachypnoea or borderline blood pressure, but the benefit is fewer decompensations (half of control-arm events were a NEWS of 9 or more alone), not fewer deaths.
For the failing RV, be cautious with fluid, start noradrenaline early, prefer high-flow oxygen and treat intubation as a peri-arrest procedure.
Know your local pathway (PERT, catheter therapy, surgery and VA-ECMO) and how to reach it out of hours.
Watch for PEITHO-3 (reduced-dose alteplase), PEERLESS II and PERSEVERE (thrombectomy in high-risk PE).
